cases.subtitle_text: Achieving Significant Growth Across Organic Search and LinkedIn
cases.about_text: Duracube, a leading provider of wet area joinery solutions, engaged in a comprehensive digital marketing strategy to enhance its online presence, drive traffic, and increase conversions. Its buyers include architects, designers, builders and project managers. This case study outlines the challenges faced, solutions implemented, and results achieved across organic search, the website and LinkedIn Ads.
cases.facts_html:
Industry
Wet area joinery for commercial projects
Location
Australia
Channels
SEO, CRO and LinkedIn Ads
Objective
Organic visibility, conversions and specifier reach
cases.challenge_html:
1. Keyword Targeting and SEO Optimisation: Duracube needed to optimise its content for a diverse set of keywords related to bathroom and toilet partitions, compact laminate, and accessibility standards, ensuring visibility across various search terms.
  2. Technical SEO and Site Structure: Ensuring the website was technically sound, with optimised meta tags, schema markup, and a logical site structure to improve search engine rankings and user experience.
  3. Content and Local SEO: Creating relevant content that addresses the needs of local audiences in multiple regions, including Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane, and Adelaide.
  4. Analytics and Performance Monitoring: Implementing effective tracking and analysis of web traffic and user behaviour to continually refine the marketing strategy.
  5. Reaching Specifiers on LinkedIn: Duracube wanted to promote its Specifier Portal to senior people in architecture, design and building management. Its first LinkedIn campaigns used static and carousel ads optimised for website conversions, running at a 0.53% click-through rate and $1.95 per click.

sol2.label: LinkedIn Ads
sol2.intro: On LinkedIn, Digilari changed the format, the bidding and the targeting:

boxes.title: Video-first creative
boxes.description:
• Replaced static and carousel ads with single video Sponsored Content: specifier-focused videos promoting the 15-year warranty and architect-ready tools such as Revit BIM models, then launch videos for the new First Nations Range.
  • The best videos reached a 6.2% to 7.5% click-through rate.

boxes.title: Click-focused bidding
boxes.description: • Switched from conversion bidding, which had too little data to learn from, to landing page click optimisation so LinkedIn could find the people most likely to visit.

boxes.title: Senior decision-maker targeting
boxes.description:
• Targeted 17 job titles at Senior, Manager, Director, Partner and Owner level, layered with relevant skills, industries and fields of study such as architecture.
  • Companies with 1 to 10 staff and competitor employees were excluded.

boxes.title: Sector pages and tighter seniority
boxes.description: • In October 2026, targeting moved to job function and Manager-and-above seniority at companies with 51 or more staff, sending people to industrial, commercial and sports facility pages.

results2.title: Nine Times the Click-Through Rate at Less Than Half the Cost per Click
results2.editor:
1. Click-through rate:
    • Up from 0.53% to 4.97% on the video campaign.
  2. Cost per click:
    • Down 58%, from $1.95 to $0.82.
  3. Website clicks:
    • 83% more clicks (7,237 against 3,961) on 24% less spend ($5,860 against $7,716).
  4. Sector pages:
    • The refined October 2026 campaign is running at a 3.89% click-through rate and $0.72 per click.

cases.subtitle_text: Harvesting Growth with Targeted Paid Ads Across Google and Meta
cases.about_text: Nestled in Australia’s Northern Rivers, Three Springs Farm is a certified organic producer with a focus on medicinal herbs and sustainable farming. Their flagship product, Complete•3 Turmeric Liquid Extract, reflects their commitment to a “food as medicine” philosophy, bringing together traditional knowledge and scientific backing to promote health. Digilari manages its paid advertising on both Google and Meta: Google captures people already searching, while Meta finds new customers likely to buy.
cases.facts_html:
Industry
Certified organic herbs
Location
Northern Rivers, Australia
Channels
Google Ads and Meta Ads (Facebook and Instagram)
Objective
Online sales
cases.challenge_html:
1. Google Ads: Three Springs Farm faced substantial obstacles in digital advertising, primarily due to high conversion costs that restricted ad visibility and effectiveness. The challenge was twofold: enhancing ad delivery to reach a wider yet targeted audience within a tight budget, and addressing gaps in online customer engagement.
  2. Meta Ads: With a fixed budget of $300 a month, Meta needed to bring in new customers profitably, not just traffic. The previous Meta campaign was already returning 6.92x, so the task was to keep finding new buyers across Australia without letting the cost per purchase climb.

sol2.label: Meta Ads
sol2.intro: On Meta, Digilari focused spend on people close to buying and kept testing the creative:

boxes.title: Near-buyer audiences
boxes.description:
• The main prospecting ad set targeted health, wellness, organic food, fitness and gardening interests, with recent buyers excluded so budget went to new customers.
  • It was refined over time into a 3% lookalike of people who added to cart but didn't buy, and took 85% of spend for 291 orders at 7.53x.

boxes.title: Credibility and offer-led creative
boxes.description:
• Single image ads and a 10-card carousel led with the product's credentials (certified organic, grown on the family farm) and the subscription and free-delivery offers.
  • The carousel returned 10.2x.

boxes.title: Seasonal Christmas push
boxes.description:
• A separate, time-limited ad set promoted the returning 500ml bottle for Christmas, optimised to checkouts.
  • It delivered 47 orders at 7.38x.

boxes.title: Facebook and Instagram together
boxes.description:
• The campaign ran across both placements and let Meta allocate spend.
  • Instagram took 12% of spend and returned 14.4x, against 6.5x on Facebook.
  • A September 2025 creative refresh with subscription-saving messaging reached 16.5x.

results2.title: Meta-Attributed Sales at a 7.5x Return on Ad Spend
results2.editor:
1. Revenue:
    • $33,062 in Meta-attributed online sales from $4,404 in ad spend over 15 months (December 2024 to February 2026).
  2. Orders:
    • 338 orders at $13.03 each, with average order value up from $90.04 to $97.82.
  3. Return on ad spend:
    • 7.51x, up from 6.92x on the previous campaign. Instagram placements returned 14.4x.
  4. Best month:
    • April 2025, with 44 orders and $4,735 in revenue from $299 in spend (15.8x).

cases.extra_html:
The ads behind the results

What changed and when

  1. OngoingMonthly budget held at $300, with daily budgets reviewed and adjusted weekly.
  2. Jun 2025Reviewed targeting, budgets and creative, and adjusted Advantage+ creative settings.
  3. Aug 2025Fixed audience targeting after a Meta audience update removed some segments, and enabled Advantage+ creative adjustments.
  4. Sep 2025Refreshed the creative with subscription-saving messaging.
  5. Nov 2025Created a 3% lookalike audience and narrowed the broad targeting.
  6. Feb 2026Moved to a new campaign that also retargets people who added to cart without buying in the previous 90 days.
